name: tutorial-steps-visual
description: Step-by-step visual walkthrough of all 23 tutorial steps (0-22) with per-step screenshots for visual regression testing. Exercises the tutorial overlay from start through congratulations, capturing each step's UI state, highlight targets, and progress indicator. Every player-facing step is a real click gated by the tutorial's own rail (issue #479/Finding #74 follow-up), including the box-cut and haul-debris stages the file originally skipped entirely.

expect.note: tutorial_pit grants $80,000 starting cash on a 32x20x32 grid (Level.ts)

steps.description: tutorial_start now has a base registration in createRunner() (issue #585) alongside its richer, DOM/overlay-driven override in src/main.ts (last-write-wins on the same runner, so the browser path is unaffected) -- command mode genuinely sets `isPaused = true` here too, same as interaction mode's real handler. The added waitForSelector/waitForTutorialStep only run in interaction mode (command mode has no overlay to wait on) and gate every real click below on the rail actually being armed, mirroring tutorial-interactive.json. Because command mode now really pauses here, every `tick N` step below only ever advances one real tick per call regardless of N (tickCommand's own loop breaks on `state.isPaused`, events.ts) -- the cash figures on the pre-blast tick steps are calibrated for that real, single-tick-per-call behavior, not the N the command text names.

steps.description: Start corrected from the file's original 15,15 to 20,20 (Finding #74/#75 follow-up): the tutorial's drill-plan stage gates its picker to REGION.drill, the exact rectangle (20,20)-(30,30) (tutorialStages.ts). spacing and depth both corrected from the file's original 5/8 to the grid tool's real defaults 3/6 (DEFAULT_SPACING_M/DEFAULT_DEPTH_M, Drill.ts), discovered live: neither stepper (#bs-param-strip [data-field="spacing"|"depth"]) is one of this stage's own targets (tutorialStages.ts's 'drill-plan' entry lists only the toolbar, grid-tool button, and picker canvas/confirm) -- the tutorial rail's own CSS lockout makes every other control pointer-events:none while a stage is active, confirmed by two real interaction-mode failures in a row (depth stepper, then a wrong 16-hole count once depth was fixed but spacing was still assumed adjustable). A real playthrough of this tutorial stage cannot reach any grid but the raw-default one for whatever rectangle is dragged: (30-20)/3+1 = 4 holes per side = 16 total, not the file's original declared 9. Matches tutorial-interactive.json's drill-plan step, which already used the real depth default for the same reason (it did not attempt a non-default spacing at all).

This step's own explosive/amount/stemming already match the Charge panel's real defaults (boomite/5kg/2m, confirmed throughout this suite's Finding #10 audit) so the click reproduces the declared command exactly, unlike most other files' charge steps. tutorial_start (step 2) arms the tutorial rail (tutorialStages.ts): a control not on the current stage is inert, so every player-facing step below is a real click gated by waitForTutorialStep, matching tutorial-interactive.json's proven pattern.

blast complete: Execute clicked, confirm dialog answered, Blast Report closed. deathCount raised 1 -> 2 (#558 full-disc survey claim follow-up, issue #558/PR #569): step 5's `survey seismic x:23 z:23` claims its full SURVEY_COVERAGE_RADIUS=20 disc (siteExpansion.ts's cellsInDisc), growing the site from the starting 32x32 to 48x48 before the driller is hired at step 10. Employee hire's spawn point is `minX + sizeX/2, minZ + sizeZ/2` -- on this run minX/minZ stay 0 throughout (the site only grows eastward/southward from (0,0), never crosses into negative territory), so that formula numerically equals the pre-#571 `sizeX/2` here; this scenario's deathCount:2 reproduces identically whether or not the #571 origin-offset fix is applied and is NOT evidence for that fix (verified live, both ways). The real driver is #558's site growth alone: on the grown 48x48 site the spawn point resolves to (26, 24), which lands inside this step's own 4x4/spacing-3 drill grid (x:20-29, z:20-29). Verified live by direct reproduction (both employees' positions and post-blast alive state read from a real run of this exact command sequence): Walt Dusty (surveyor) ends the survey task at (23, 23), Kurt Hardhat (driller) sits idle at the grid-centre spawn point (26, 24), and this drill plan's CATASTROPHIC-rated blast (furthest throw 27.9m) kills both via the same fragment-kinetic-energy check (Damage.ts's processEmployeeHit) -- a real, physically-grounded double death, not a miscalculation. cash is unaffected either way (lawsuits/fines from a death do not deduct immediately). The #571 origin-offset regression itself is covered separately by the unit/integration tests added in 75a06cf, which force a negative origin (x:-4, z:-4).

The file's original decreased:["safety"] assertion does not survive across both modes (Finding #74/#75 follow-up, discovered live) -- not because the point is wrong, but because it is no longer independently checkable here. In command mode safety still drops exactly on this scripted tick (50 -> 45.05, matching the file's original point precisely). In interaction mode the blast step's own waitForTutorialStep (stepId: ["scores","event-fire-resolve","hire-manager"]) drives the real clock through several ticks while polling for the rail to reach hire-manager -- including the event-fire-resolve stage's own autoCommands: ["tick 3", ...] -- so the safety damage already lands during that wait, before this step ever runs, and by here it reads 35.15 with nothing left to decrease on this specific tick. Same class as the contract-deliver step below: real per-click waiting does not reproduce command mode's precise scripted tick count. cash is unaffected by either mode's path and stays checkable.

contract-accept complete: Accept clicked on the first offer in the Contracts panel. tutorial_start (step 2) arms the tutorial rail (tutorialStages.ts): a control not on the current stage is inert, so every player-facing step below is a real click gated by waitForTutorialStep, matching tutorial-interactive.json's proven pattern. #513/#581: the accept click is scoped to `[data-contract-id="1"]`, the contract this step's `command` names. Unscoped, `.bs-contract-accept` always resolves to whichever offered card is first in the DOM, so command mode accepted contract #1 literally while interaction mode accepted whatever led the list -- two channels driving different contracts while both reported pass, because nothing asserted here can tell them apart (`activeContractCount` counts accepts, not identities). `level1-win-efficient` is what that costs once a `[data-contract-id]`-scoped assertion is added on top: its guard failed with its control absent from the DOM entirely, red on `main`, cause pointing nowhere near the accept step. ContractsPanel sets `data-contract-id` on offered cards (`makeOfferedCard`), so scoping removes the DOM-order coupling rather than baking around it.

Same divergence tutorial-interactive.json already documents for the identical reason (command mode's automatic dispatch needs real ticks it never gets between the haul-debris step's single tick and this one, so command mode and interaction mode read genuinely different outcomes here). Not asserted with an exact equals here, matching tutorial-interactive.json's own contract-deliver step: the waitForTutorialStep gate above is itself the proof of completion (the tutorial's own isComplete requires completedHistory to grow), and the exact delivered tonnage is position/timing-dependent, the same reasoning hauling-gate.json documents (Finding #33).
